content.value_statement: Multi-agent systems can waste tokens, add latency, and fail without clear coordination metrics. This skill guides profiling, workload distribution, cost controls, and validation plans for reliable orchestration.
actual_capabilities: Defines baseline metrics and target performance goals before optimization.
Maps database, application, and frontend profiling agents for bottleneck analysis.
Recommends context compression, token budgets, caching, and model selection controls.
Outlines parallel execution, workload partitioning, and fault-tolerant coordination patterns.
Provides staged workflows for e-commerce and enterprise API optimization.
limitations: It offers guidance and examples, not a runnable orchestration framework.
It requires existing metrics, logs, or evaluations to produce useful recommendations.
It does not validate changes against a live environment automatically.
It assumes the user can define budget and quality constraints.

use_cases.title: Improve Agent Workflow Throughput
use_cases.description: Profile coordination bottlenecks and design a staged plan to reduce latency across agent handoffs.

use_cases.title: Control LLM Operating Costs
use_cases.description: Set token budgets, model selection rules, and caching policies for recurring multi-agent tasks.

use_cases.title: Plan Performance Regression Testing
use_cases.description: Define validation metrics and rollback checks before deploying orchestration changes.

prompt_templates.title: Profile a Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Profile my multi-agent workflow. Target: [system]. Goals: [metrics]. Current metrics: [data]. Recommend low-risk improvements and validation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Reduce Token Costs
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this agent workflow for token waste. Budget: [limit]. Quality threshold: [threshold]. Suggest context compression, caching, and model routing changes.

prompt_templates.title: Improve Coordination
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a coordination plan for these agents: [agents]. Workload: [tasks]. Constraints: [latency, reliability, cost]. Include risks and rollback checks.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize an Enterprise Rollout
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a phased optimization plan for [system]. Include profiling agents, workload distribution, cost controls, quality gates, rollout stages, and monitoring metrics.

output_examples.input: A support automation workflow has slow triage, repeated context, and rising model costs.
output_examples.output: The skill would recommend baseline latency metrics, context filtering, cached summaries, lower-cost routing for simple tickets, and staged regression tests.

output_examples.input: An API analysis workflow uses database, backend, and frontend agents with unclear handoff delays.
output_examples.output: The skill would map each agent responsibility, identify handoff bottlenecks, propose parallel execution, and define rollback metrics.

output_examples.input: A team wants to deploy orchestration changes without harming answer quality.
output_examples.output: The skill would define quality thresholds, compare before-and-after results, and recommend gradual rollout with monitoring.

best_practices: Set baseline metrics before changing coordination, context, or model selection.
Apply one optimization at a time and measure the result before the next change.
Keep rollback plans for routing, caching, and parallel execution changes.
anti_patterns: Do not optimize without measurable goals, logs, or evaluation data.
Do not deploy orchestration changes directly to production without regression tests.
Do not reduce context or model quality without checking task accuracy.

faq.question: Does this skill run optimization scripts?
faq.answer: No. It provides structured guidance, planning prompts, and illustrative examples for human-reviewed optimization work.

faq.question: Which tools does it support?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Can it help reduce LLM costs?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers token budgets, model selection, caching, and result reuse for multi-agent workflows.

faq.question: What inputs should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the target system, performance goals, optimization scope, budget constraints, and quality metrics.

faq.question: Is it suitable for single-agent prompt tuning?
faq.answer: No. It is intended for workflows that involve multiple agents and coordination concerns.

faq.question: Does it replace performance testing?
faq.answer: No. It recommends validation plans, but production changes still need environment-specific tests.
